gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured capacity for any of its picks: techtest.org's electronic-load tests put the LiTime 12V 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth at 102.46 Ah average (100.92 to 103.33 Ah, 30 to 40 A discharge), the standard LiTime 12V 100Ah at 106.06 Ah, Vatrer 12V 100Ah at 104.2 Ah and Redodo 12V 100Ah at 107.7 Ah, all above the 100 Ah rating, while Will Prowse's controlled test of a Battle Born 75 Ah had the BMS repeatedly disconnecting after 14 cycles at 49 A.
standout_why: Both cited rivals disclaim testing. BatteryTrail's spec database says outright 'We did not test batteries ourselves for this page' and sources every figure to manufacturer pages or an Amazon listing; ExploringOffGrid says its picks were 'shortlisted from manufacturer spec sheets and manuals' and gives no measured figure. ChatGPT's own answer says 'These are current listings, not results of my own battery testing.' None of the 13 results names a measured Ah, a cycle-test datapoint or a load-test failure. techtest.org's 22-battery measured-capacity table (19 Oct 2026), its per-model load tests, Panbo's ongoing 600-cycle test and the Hackaday write-ups of Will Prowse's Battle Born tests are all absent.
decides: Confirms LiTime as the value pick with a number instead of a spec sheet: every LiTime 100Ah variant techtest measured delivered 101.6 to 106.1 Ah, and the Group 24 Bluetooth model ChatGPT led with delivered 102.5 Ah average even at 30 A and 100.9 Ah at 40 A. It undercuts the 'premium, buy for support' framing of Battle Born: Will Prowse's teardown of a 100 Ah unit found the positive terminal loosely attached to the bus bar with a melted spacer, and his controlled 49 A cycling of a 75 Ah unit produced repeated BMS disconnects after 14 cycles, with Dragonfly Energy (Battle Born's parent) now suing him over the videos. The cheapest candidate in Dealectric's catalog, Redodo 12V 100Ah, has the highest measured capacity of the group at 107.7 Ah, and Vatrer 12V 100Ah measured 104.2 Ah, so both can be recommended on measured data rather than brand reputation.
